_readme: The interactive vocabulary for Phase 3. Ten reusable, data-driven templates.
A chapter's interactive declares a template name and the data that fills it;
nobody builds a bespoke game for a chapter. build_assets.py validates each
chapter's data against the shape declared here and refuses to write if it
does not fit, so a template typo is an error rather than a blank panel.
Adding a template is a real decision, not a shortcut around awkward data:
if a chapter does not fit any of the ten, the honest move is usually to pick
the nearest fit and simplify the content, because every new template is a
new front-end component to build, test and maintain.

match-pairs.what: Two columns to be paired up. The match-the-column question type the papers already use.
match-pairs.suits: term and definition, person and work, god and domain, kingdom and capital, scientist and discovery

timeline-order.what: Drag items into the right order. Order can be chronological or procedural.
timeline-order.suits: history dates, the stages of a process, the accounting cycle, the steps of cell division

data.items: list[3..8] of {label: str, note: str?}  — authored in the CORRECT order; the front end shuffles

sort-bins.what: Drop each item into one of a few labelled bins.
sort-bins.suits: renewable vs non-renewable, assets vs liabilities, metals vs non-metals, direct vs indirect tax

data.items: list[4..12] of {label: str, bin: str}  — bin must name one of bins

odd-one-out.what: Four or five items, one of which does not belong, and the child must say which.
odd-one-out.suits: classification, spotting the exception, any 'which of these is not a...' idea

data.because: str  — the rule the other items share

fill-blank.what: A short passage with gaps, filled from a shared word bank. The bank may hold decoys.
fill-blank.suits: grammar, definitions, formulae stated in words, any paragraph of connected fact

data.text: str  — gaps written as {1}, {2}, ... numbered from 1
data.bank: list of str  — must contain every answer, and may contain decoys

transform.what: Rewrite a given sentence under a stated rule, then compare against the model answer.
transform.suits: active and passive, direct and indirect speech, tense change, degree of comparison

data.rule: str  — the transformation being practised, e.g. 'Change to passive voice'
data.items: list[2..8] of {from: str, to: str, hint: str?}

label-diagram.what: Place labels onto a diagram at given points. The diagram is an inline SVG stored with the asset.
label-diagram.suits: cell parts, the human eye, a circuit, map features, an account format

data.svg: str  — self-contained inline SVG, viewBox 0 0 100 100, no external refs
data.labels: list[2..8] of {label: str, x: num 0..100, y: num 0..100}

formula-pick.what: Given a quantity or situation, choose the formula that applies, and see why the others do not.
formula-pick.suits: physics quantities, mensuration, cost sheets, ratio analysis

data.items: list[2..6] of {ask: str, correct: str, wrong: list[1..3] of str, why: str}

step-solve.what: One worked problem advanced a step at a time; the child picks the next step before seeing it.
step-solve.suits: any numerical — maths, physics, accountancy, cost sheets

data.steps: list[2..6] of {ask: str, options: list[2..4] of str, correct: int, why: str}

true-false.what: A short set of statements to mark true or false, each with a one-line reason either way.
true-false.suits: the universal fallback — any chapter whose content resists the other nine

data.items: list[3..8] of {statement: str, is_true: bool, why: str}
